chunks: And Al-Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, who elevated it (mursal), saying:

Abu Hanifa left from the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) was standing there — he being a young boy. Abu Hanifa said to him: 'O young boy, where does a stranger relieve himself in your town?'

He said: 'Avoid the courtyards of mosques, the banks of rivers, the places where fruits fall, and the resting places of travelers; do not face the qibla with stool or urine; raise your garment and relieve yourself wherever you wish.'

key_terms.أَفْنِيَةَ: courtyards/forecourts — the open spaces immediately surrounding mosques, forbidden for relieving oneself
key_terms.اَلْقِبْلَةَ: the qibla — direction of prayer toward Mecca; facing it during defecation or urination is prohibited
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: he elevated it (rafa'ahu) — technical hadith term indicating a mursal transmission with the intermediate chain omitted
key_terms.شُطُوطَ: banks/shores — the edges of rivers, likewise forbidden
key_terms.مَسَاقِطَ اَلثِّمَارِ: fruit-drop zones — places beneath fruit trees where fallen produce is gathered, forbidden due to public use

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic etiquette rules for relieving oneself, according to Imam Musa al-Kazim in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter in which Abu Hanifa — upon leaving the presence of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) — found the young Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) standing outside and asked him where a stranger might relieve himself in their town. The boy Imam's compact answer enumerated five forbidden sites (mosque courtyards, riverbanks, fruit-drop areas, travelers' resting places, and facing the qibla) and then granted broad permissibility elsewhere, demonstrating his precocious jurisprudential mastery. The incident is transmitted as a mursal (rafa'ahu) hadith, meaning the intermediate links between Ali ibn Ibrahim and the Imam are not specified.
